coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED (in order of reliability):

(1) 2015 Alabama Football Media Guide (published July 29, 2015), archived PDF: https://web.archive.org/web/20160313043706/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/alab/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2015-16/misc_non_event/20150729MFBmedia-guide.pdf — this is the single most complete source. Its "coaches and staff" section runs PDF pages 76-93 (printed pp. 71-88) and ends with a full support-staff photo grid on PDF p. 93 (printed p. 88) listing 35 support staff with titles. Because it is a PDF whose staff grid is a multi-column layout, I set quote to "" for all media-guide-only rows per instructions. I did NOT eyeball these: I extracted the page's text blocks with x/y coordinates (PyMuPDF) and confirmed every name-to-title pairing by column position, so the pairings are verified, not inferred.

(2) rolltide.com official football coaches page captured by the Wayback Machine DURING the 2015 season — Dec 6, 2015 (https://web.archive.org/web/20151206214105/http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/coaches.html) and Nov 16, 2015 (…/20151116051021/…). Both captures are identical and list the same 13 (10 on-field + Cochran + Dickens + Wright). Quotes from this page are the true plain-text rendering: the name is a link and the title is the next text node, so the verbatim string is "Name\nTitle" (newline between). If the checker fetches raw HTML instead of rendered text, these will need whitespace-insensitive matching.

(3) Wikipedia, cited via the raw-wikitext URL rather than the rendered article, so the quoted table rows are guaranteed byte-present in what is fetched.

(4) Roll 'Bama Roll (SB Nation) 2022 retrospective, used as a secondary corroborating source for off-field staff. Note it explicitly says its off-field list is "not a complete list." Its table quotes are also "Name\nRole" plain-text form.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT / CAVEATS:

- The media guide was published July 29, 2015. Any support-staff person hired between August 2015 and the Jan. 11, 2016 championship game would not appear in it, and I found no in-season staff-addition announcements for 2015. There is no Wayback capture of a full Alabama football SUPPORT-staff directory near the title date — the archived in-season rolltide coaches page lists only the 13 on-field/major staff, not analysts or GAs. So the 35 support-staff rows are documented as of preseason 2015, not as of the championship game. I could not verify individually that each of them was still employed on Jan. 11, 2016.
- I could NOT find documentation of any mid-season departure. Bo Davis left for Texas after the season (Feb. 2016), so he was on staff for the title game.
- Explicitly EXCLUDED, despite being commonly misremembered as 2015 Alabama staff: Steve Sarkisian. He was fired by USC in Oct. 2015 but was not hired by Alabama until September 2016; he was an analyst for the 2016 season, not 2015. Also excluded: Jeremy Pruitt (Georgia DC in 2015, arrived at Alabama in 2016), Mike Locksley (arrived 2016), Brent Key (his rolltide bio page first appears in the archive in Feb. 2016).
- Titles in the media guide grid are printed in ALL CAPS; I have preserved the wording exactly but normalized capitalization to title case.
- Name spellings printed by the media guide that appear to be typos and which I corrected, with the printed form recorded in the source note: "ERIC KEISAU" (the analyst is Eric Kiesau — Roll 'Bama Roll independently lists him as "Eric Kiesau, Analyst") and "AAZAAR A. RAHIM" (Aazaar Abdul-Rahim).
- Rodney Brown is documented only by a prose line in the media guide's training-room page (PDF p. 105) naming the full-time football athletic training staff; he has no photo/title entry, so his exact title is not documented beyond "athletic trainer."
- The current live rolltide.com page at /sports/football/coaches/2015 is NOT reliable for this season: it lists only 9 people and attaches later titles to them (e.g. Mario Cristobal as "Assistant Head Coach/Tackles and Tight Ends/Recruiting Coordinator" and Bobby Williams as "Special Assistant to the Head Coach," both of which are his 2016 title), and it omits Smart, Tucker, Davis and Cochran entirely. I did not use it as a role source.
- No one on the 2015 staff carried a "quality control" title; Alabama used "analyst" for that tier, so the qc category is empty by design.
- Total documented: 56 people. Nothing in this list is inferred or padded — every row traces to the media guide, the in-season school coaches page, Wikipedia, or Roll 'Bama Roll.
